tagline.text: The Philippines' Longest Sea-Crossing Cable-Stayed Bridge, Linking Cebu and Cordova

location.label: Location
location.text: Mactan Channel, between South Road Properties in Cebu City and Cordova on Mactan Island

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (December–May dry season is most pleasant)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱0–500 (per person, vehicle toll and transport included; the walking lane is free)

children.text: The Cebu-Cordova Link Expressway (CCLEX) is a toll sea bridge about 8.9km long that opened in April 2022, and it is billed as the longest bridge over the sea in the Philippines. Thanks to its cable-stayed section with twin pylons, it is also popular for views of the Mactan Channel and for night scenery.

The Cebu-Cordova Link Expressway (CCLEX) is a toll bridge that crosses the Mactan Channel from South Road Properties (SRP), a reclaimed area south of Cebu City, to Cordova at the southern end of Mactan Island. It is about
8.9km

long, has four lanes and is roughly 27m wide. It is described as the longest sea-crossing bridge in the Philippines, and because it is the third bridge linking Cebu City and Mactan Island, it is also known as the Third Cebu-Mactan Bridge. The total project cost is reported to be about ₱33 billion.
The heart of the bridge is its cable-stayed section. The main span between the two pylons is about
, and the twin pylons stand about
tall. The deck sits about

above the water so that large ships can pass beneath. The pylons were designed with inspiration from the Magellan's Cross pavilion, a symbol of Cebu City, and near the tops are eight "Iconic Crosses" that are lit at night. Construction began in March 2017, the bridge was inaugurated on April 27, 2022, and general traffic began on April 30, 2022. It is operated by CCLEX Corporation, a subsidiary of Metro Pacific Tollways.

There are two reasons this bridge matters to travelers. First, it directly links Cordova in the south of Mactan Island with the southern coast of Cebu City (SRP and the Cebu South Coastal Road), so it works as a bypass when the two older bridges in northern Mactan are congested. Second, it is one of the few places that people visit simply to see a bridge. You can take in the sea and the Cebu City skyline in one view, and the pylons are lit at night. According to some reports and notices, there is a free walking and cycling lane separated from the traffic lanes, so you can also experience crossing on foot. However, the operating hours and entry rules for the walking and cycling lane can change, so check the latest announcement before you go.

This guide is for travelers staying in Cebu who plan to use or visit the bridge within a day or two. If you are heading from the airport to a hotel in northern Mactan, CCLEX may not be faster. Because the bridge lands at the southern tip of Mactan Island (Cordova), it is most useful for reaching resorts in Cordova and southern Mactan, or for traveling to and from Cebu City's southern coast (SRP and the South Coastal Road). Toll rates and the rules for the walking section have changed recently, so it is safest to confirm them again locally.
The face of the bridge is its twin pylons, about
tall, and the cables that run between them. The main span between the pylons is about
, and the deck is about
above sea level so that large ships can pass. It is hard to appreciate from inside a car, so look up at it from a distance along the shore to feel its scale.

blocks.title: Pylons Inspired by Magellan's Cross, and Eight Crosses

children.text: The pylons are said to have been designed with inspiration from the Magellan's Cross pavilion in Cebu City. The eight Iconic Crosses near the tops are lit, so after dark they stand out from almost anywhere along the Mactan Channel. Seeing them together with Magellan's Cross in Cebu City ties the story together.
At about
8.9km

in total length, it is billed as the longest sea-crossing bridge in the Philippines. That figure covers not only the cable-stayed section but also the long approach viaducts and the over-water roadway on both sides. Locals often mention that travel time from Cebu City to Cordova dropped considerably after it opened.
A pedestrian and bicycle lane separated from the roadway is reported to exist, and it is described as free to use. At the design stage, the width on each side was reported as about
. Entry points and opening hours can change, so check the official CCLEX announcements before you go. There is almost no shade, so bring water and a hat.

At dusk you can see the Cebu City skyline across the channel together with the lit pylons. Viewing from a distance along the Cordova shore or the SRP shore is the most straightforward option. A plan to walk across at night may not work because of the opening hours of the walking section, so check the times in advance.

blocks.title: Access to Cordova and Southern Mactan

children.text: The Mactan end of the bridge meets Babag II Road near Pilipog and Ibabao in Cordova. When you head to resorts in Cordova or to the south of Lapu-Lapu City, it gives you a direct route without using the northern bridges. It is far from the airport, so allow plenty of time if your flight schedule is tight.

blocks.title: Electronic Tolls and the Artificial-Island Toll Plaza

children.text: The toll plaza is a single barrier plaza built on an artificial island at sea, and its design is said to reflect the eight-rayed sun of the Philippine flag. Electronic toll collection started on July 2, 2022. Cash lanes can be congested, so many rental cars and commercial vehicles carry an RFID sticker.

items.title: Half-Day Sightseeing Route
items.subtitle: Drive across and enjoy the view from the shore

children.text: Set out from the SRP side of Cebu City. If you take a taxi or Grab, the
toll is often added to the fare for the passenger
, so confirm whether it is included before you ride.
Pass the CCLEX toll plaza and cross toward Cordova. The crossing by car usually takes around
10 minutes
, but it takes longer if the plaza on the Cordova side is crowded.
Find a spot on the Cordova shore or near the connecting road where the pylons are visible and take photos. Do not enter private property or restricted areas.
Enjoy the sunset sky and the pylons. The view changes noticeably once the pylon lights come on.
Have dinner in Cordova and return the same way, or head north on Mactan and cross the Marcelo Fernan Bridge back to your lodging.
Sunset time changes with the season, so check the sunset time before you leave.

items.title: Crossing on Foot
items.subtitle: Using the walking and cycling lane

children.text: Check the official notices on whether the walking and cycling lane is open and its hours. Some notices say it opens at 6 a.m. and closes in the afternoon with an early last entry, but this can change, so always check the latest announcement.
Start walking from the entrance on the Cordova side. There is no shade, so prepare water, a hat and sunscreen.
Near the pylons, enjoy the view of the Mactan Channel and toward Cebu City, and take photos. Walking the whole length takes a long time, so many people turn back near the pylons.
Return to Cordova and have a combined breakfast and lunch.
Drones, small-wheeled devices (skateboards, kick scooters), pets and fishing rods are reported to be prohibited. Follow the signs on site.
A nonstop flight from Manila (NAIA) to Mactan–Cebu International Airport (CEB) takes about
1 hour 20 minutes
. There are several flights a day, so check the latest schedule.
CEB Airport is in the north of Mactan Island. CCLEX lands at Cordova in the south of the island, so it is not a direct route from the airport.
From central Cebu City, head toward SRP, pass the CCLEX toll plaza and cross to Cordova. If you use a taxi or Grab, first confirm how the toll is handled.
Rental cars pay at the toll plaza with RFID or cash. You pay again when you come back the same way.
From the Mactan side, follow the signs toward Cordova to the CCLEX approach. The road connects to the bridge near Babag II Road.
When going from the airport area to Cebu City, the Marcelo Fernan Bridge in northern Mactan is often closer, so choose according to your destination.
To cross on foot, use the entrance on the Cordova side. On the Cebu City side, a footbridge of about
is reported to connect to the sidewalk of the South Coastal Road on-ramp.
Check the opening hours and entry points in the official notices.
Some motorcycles are allowed but there is an engine-size limit, and tricycles are reported not to be permitted.
The bridge is open to traffic all year. For walking across or taking photos from the shore, the drier season is more comfortable.
The walking section has no shade and is very hot at midday. Plan for early morning or sunset, but check the walking section's opening hours first.

CCLEX itself has no lodging or restaurants. There are resorts in Cordova and along the southern Mactan coast, and on the Cebu City side you can use the malls and dining areas around SRP. Seeing the bridge and then having dinner nearby works well.

The Cordova coastal village has seafood restaurants and small local eateries. Prices vary a lot from place to place, so check the menu first. It is easiest to sleep at a resort on Mactan or a hotel in Cebu City and fit this bridge into a one-day itinerary.
The toll table reflects the October 2025 increase. It can change, so check the latest announcement.
With an RFID tag, a rental car can avoid waiting in the cash lanes. The Cordova side is said to get crowded on Sunday afternoons.
The walking section has no shade, so be sure to bring water, a hat and sunscreen.
Flying drones is reported to be prohibited, so do not fly one.
When going to the airport or to northern Mactan, choose whichever of CCLEX or the Marcelo Fernan Bridge is closer to your destination.
Passengers often end up paying the toll in a taxi or Grab, so mention it before you ride.
For sunset photos, find a spot on the Cordova shore where the pylons are visible, and do not enter private property or restricted areas.
On days with a fixed schedule, leave extra time. Toll plaza congestion or restrictions can lengthen travel time.
The walking and cycling lane's hours and rules can change, and you must not stop on the roadway to take photos. Always follow the signs on site and the latest announcements.
This is an expressway section, so vehicles must not stop on the shoulder or in a lane to take photos.
Small motorcycles (under 110cc) and tricycles are reported to be restricted.
On the walking section, climbing over or leaning on railings, making U-turns, drinking alcohol, flying drones, fishing and flying kites are reported to be prohibited.
The walking section has no shade and can be windy, so watch out for heat and dehydration.
In the rainy season or typhoons there may be closures or changes in operation, so check the announcements.
The island where the Mactan end of the bridge lands, with many resorts and beaches. Heading north from Cordova takes you to central Lapu-Lapu City and the airport.
A memorial area honoring Lapulapu, and a good addition to a Mactan Island itinerary.
A historic site in Cebu City that is worth seeing alongside the CCLEX pylon design.
The city at the Cebu end of the bridge, close to the malls around SRP and the downtown attractions.
